help.title: Help
help.subtitle: How to use Hakufu, in eight steps
help.s1.title: Getting started
help.s1.intro: Hakufu organizes and reads the manga you already have on your computer. All it needs to know is which folder they're in.
help.s1.t1.text: Go to Settings → Library folder and click “Choose folder…”. Pick the folder where you keep your manga.
help.s1.t2.text: Each subfolder is a collection (a series), and the PDF, CBR or CBZ files inside it are its volumes.
help.s1.t3.text: All your collections show up there with their covers. You're ready to read.
help.s1.outro: Hakufu doesn't copy or move anything: it reads the folder as it is. To add manga, put the files in those folders (or create a new folder for a new series) and click “Refresh” in Library. Library also updates itself when you open it. Loose files in the main folder show up under “No collection”.
help.s1.tip: Settings → Library folder also has “Open folder”, which opens it in your file explorer, and “Rescan”, which goes through the whole folder again.
help.s2.title: Library and collections
help.s2.intro: Each collection is a pile of covers, like volumes stacked on a shelf. Underneath, how many volumes it has and how far you've read.
help.s2.t1.text: Click its pile. Inside you'll see its volumes with your progress on each one: “Page 12 of 180”, “Finished”…
help.s2.t2.text: Hover over a cover and click the star. On favorites the star always stays visible. Works for collections and volumes.
help.s2.t3.text: Inside a collection: by Name, by Date or Custom (move each volume up or down with the arrows and click “Save order”). Hakufu remembers the order you choose.
help.s2.t4.text: The “Size” slider makes the covers bigger or smaller.
help.s2.t5.text: In the Library header, “Open folder” opens the library folder in your file explorer and “Refresh” reads it again so new volumes show up. Inside a collection, “Open folder” opens that collection's folder.
help.s3.title: Reading
help.s3.intro: Click a volume to open it. It opens on the page where you left off.
help.s3.t1.text: With the arrows on the bottom bar or with the keyboard (see the shortcuts below).
help.s3.t2.text: “1 page” and “2 pages” on the bottom bar. In two-page spread you see two pages side by side, like an open book.
help.s3.t3.text: “Zen” puts the reader in full screen, with no bars, just the manga. Press Esc to exit.
help.s3.t4.text: Every time you turn a page, Hakufu notes where you are. Close whenever you like with “Close”: next time you pick up right there.
help.s3.shortcuts_hint: This is how they're set now. You can change them in Settings → Keyboard shortcuts.
help.s4.title: Home
help.s4.intro: Home greets you with the last volume you were reading.
help.s4.p1: Click “Keep reading” and you're back on that exact page. If you haven't started any yet, you'll see a button to go to the library.
help.s4.p2: From the menu on the left you can reach Library, Profile, Backup, Settings and this Help.
help.s5.title: Your profile
help.s5.intro: Your reader card: how much you read, what you're reading and what you like most.
help.s5.t1.text: Add your photo, your name and your favorite manga.
help.s5.t2.text: Time spent reading, pages, finished volumes and your reading streak in days. The chart shows the hours for each of the last twelve weeks; the highlighted bar is the current week.
help.s5.t3.text: The three collections you've read most recently, with your progress on each. Click one to open it.
help.s5.t4.text: Saves the card as a PNG image to share: landscape (computer) or portrait (phone, stories).
help.s6.title: Settings
help.s6.intro: What you can change to your liking. Everything is saved instantly.
help.s6.t2.text: “Two-page spread” opens volumes at two pages from the start. “Open in zen mode” starts reading straight away in full screen.
help.s6.t3.text: Click a key and press the new one; combinations like Ctrl + W work too. Each action can have two keys. The × removes one and “Reset” brings back the defaults.
help.s6.t4.text: “Choose folder…” to change it, “Open folder” to see it in your file explorer and “Rescan” to go through it again.
help.s6.t5.text: How much space the app, your manga and Hakufu's cache (covers and data) take up.
help.s6.t6.text: Hakufu's version, and the terms and legal notice.
help.s7.title: Backup
help.s7.intro: Save everything Hakufu knows about your library to a .zip file, and restore it here or on another computer.
help.s7.t1.text: “Export backup…” creates a .zip with your profile (name, photo, stats, theme and settings) and, if you turn on “Include collections”, the progress, favorites and history of the collections you select. It stays on your computer, wherever you save it: an external drive, a USB stick or another folder.
help.s7.t2.text: Install Hakufu on the other computer, choose the library folder there (with your manga, in the same subfolders) and go to Backup → “Choose backup…”. It works across Windows, macOS and Linux. The backup doesn't include the manga files: copy them separately.
help.s7.tip: Restoring applies your profile and the progress of the volumes included in the backup; everything else stays as it is. Your manga files are never touched.
help.s8.title: Frequently asked questions
help.faq.a1: No. It reads the files straight from the library folder. If you move or delete a file there, Hakufu will notice the next time you refresh the library.
help.faq.a2: No. Hakufu works fully offline: no accounts, no servers, and nothing is sent anywhere.
help.faq.a3: On your computer, in Hakufu's data folder: reading progress, favorites, sort order, cached covers and your profile. You can open it from Backup → Open folder.
help.faq.a4: PDF, CBZ and CBR. The pages of a CBZ or CBR are sorted by each image's file name.
help.faq.q5: I added volumes and they don't show up
help.faq.a5: Make sure they're inside a subfolder of the library (each subfolder is a collection) and click “Refresh” in Library.
help.faq.q6: Can I change the reader's keys?
help.faq.a6: Yes, in Settings → Keyboard shortcuts. Each action can have up to two keys, including combinations like Ctrl + W.
help.faq.q7: How do I move everything to another computer?
help.faq.a7: Export a backup and take it along with your manga folder (the backup doesn't include the files). On the other computer, choose the library folder in Settings and import the backup. It works across Windows, macOS and Linux.
help.faq.q8: Where are the terms and legal notice?
help.faq.a8: In Settings → About → “Terms and legal notice”.
